title: The gaming PC that costs less than your phone

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: A gaming PC under $500 is possible—just look at AMD's Ryzen 5 and NVIDIA's GTX 1660 Super. Your phone can't run modern games at 4K.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Gaming isn't just about specs—it's about immersion. High refresh rate monitors, mechanical keyboards, and precise mice aren't in your phone's ecosystem.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: True, but gaming PCs use standardized protocols like USB 3.2 and HDMI 2.1. Phones are locked in with proprietary connectors and limited upgradability.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: You can't upgrade a phone's GPU or add a discrete graphics card. Gaming PCs are built for performance longevity and modularity—phones are disposable.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Your point is valid, but a phone costs less. Gaming PCs offer more value over time with upgradable components and open standards.
